title: Birbal and the Three Questions (简体中文)
summary: A foreign philosopher challenges Akbar's court with three impossible metaphysical questions. Birbal answers all three with brilliant simplicity. [ZH]
full_text:
A renowned Persian scholar and philosopher arrived at Fatehpur Sikri, carrying a scroll containing three profound philosophical riddles. Standing before Emperor Akbar, he announced:

'Your Majesty, I have tested scholars across Arabia and Persia. If your famous Raja Birbal can answer my three questions, I shall acknowledge your court as the supreme seat of wisdom in the world!'

Akbar gestured for the scholar to speak.

The scholar asked: 'First, where is the exact center of the earth?

'Second, how many stars shine in the heavens?

'And third, what is the exact number of men and women in the world?'

The assembled courtiers gasped. These questions were impossible to answer!

Birbal smiled, stood up, and requested an iron rod, a live hairy sheep from the royal pastures, and two scribes.

To answer the first question, Birbal planted the iron rod firmly into the ground in the center of the palace courtyard. 'Noble scholar, this spot where my rod stands is the exact center of the earth! If you doubt my calculation, take a measuring tape, measure around the globe in every direction, and if you find it off by even half an inch, I shall forfeit my life!'

The scholar blinked, unable to dispute the claim without measuring the entire earth.

To answer the second question, Birbal led the hairy sheep before the scholar: 'Sir, there are exactly as many stars in the sky as there are hairs upon the body of this sheep! If you doubt me, count the hairs on this sheep, and then count the stars, and see if they do not match down to the last digit!'

The scholar coughed nervously: 'How can anyone count the hairs of a sheep?'

'Just as easily as one can count the stars in the heavens!' Birbal replied with a twinkle in his eye.

'And the third question?' the scholar pressed. 'The exact number of men and women?'

Birbal replied with a playful grin: 'Sir, counting men and women would be very simple, except for one great difficulty: there are individuals like yourself who spend their lives asking pointless questions instead of doing honest work! It is impossible to tell whether such idlers should be counted as men or women! If we eliminate all useless question-askers from the census, the count of honest men and women can be completed by sunset!'

The entire court erupted in laughter, and even the Persian scholar smiled, bowing in admiration at Birbal's razor-sharp wit.
